help:
usage: dunkingsheep [-h] [--version] [--json] [--socket SOCKET]
                    [--self-pane SELF_PANE] [--no-start-daemon]
                    <command> ...

Send text into terminal panes on a schedule; control it from the keyboard, this CLI, a unix socket, or MCP.

positional arguments:
  <command>
    allocation          registered-worker automatic backlog/review allocation
    status              daemon health and counts
    turn                declare a busy turn (pi/claude hooks)
    poll                one batched read for sidebars: status + inbox + dunks
    list (ls)           list all dunks
    get                 show one dunk
    add                 create a dunk (starts immediately)
    update (set)        change a dunk's settings
    remove (rm, delete)
                        delete a dunk
    start               start a dunk
    stop                stop a dunk
    toggle              start if stopped, stop if running
    stop-all            stop every running dunk
    fire (test)         send a dunk's text now
    send                type text + Enter into a pane once (queued if someone
                        is typing)
    send-keys           press keys in a pane (queued if someone is typing)
    install             put `dunkingsheep` on PATH as a plain command
    guard               install the herdr guard (rollback backend) so agents
                        cannot type over you
    inbox               per-agent inboxes: messaging that never types
    context             declarative context store: files are truth, index is a
                        cache
    load                per-caller CPU from /proc (pid+starttime guarded,
                        process tree)
    pm                  project PMs: lane routing and the one-per-project
                        digest
    task                global and per-pane tasks: the coordination queue
    gh-token            print a one-hour App token for this lane's role (empty
                        for the owner)
    secrets-check       refuse a push/PR that would publish the desk's own
                        secrets
    git-credential      git credential helper: `git config --global
                        credential.helper '!dunkingsheep git-credential'`
    review              the review timer and its queue
    poolrad             the Poolrad backlog: backlog-sync fills it, progress
                        reads it
    github              one-shot GitHub setup with the owner's own login
    whoami              this caller's role and how it was bound
    token               service tokens for pane-less processes (web desk,
                        timers)
    superuser           who may close panes/tabs/workspaces, stop the daemon
                        or manage dunks
    memory              memory/recall over past agent sessions
    health              deterministic self-check; --repair fixes leases/WAL
    watchdog            deterministic exception watchdog (no model); --dry-run
                        sends nothing
    watchdog-deadman    alert the VP if the watchdog heartbeat is stale
                        (independent check)
    usage               real provider usage from configurable commands
    recover             post-upgrade recovery plan; --apply types into bare
                        shells
    doctor              post-upgrade doctor: backend surfaces + dunk target
                        metadata
    owner               owner -> agent delivery: pushed, never typed
    report              the deterministic fleet report (no model)
    state               continuous agent-state capture (the restartable-lane
                        record)
    roster              one row per agent lane (name, harness, state, task,
                        inbox, cpu)
    message-state       sent / delivered / seen for message ids
    reply-stats         last and median time for a lane to read its mail
    project-summary     ground truths, articles, tasks in flight, agents,
                        timeline
    api                 read-only HTTP surface for the Command Center (roster,
                        message state, project summary)
    capability (capabilities)
                        how a target can receive: push queue (pi) or immediate
                        guarded send
    lane (lanes)        the lane registry: who each pane IS, declared or
                        inferred
    retired             retired panes: kept as the record, excluded from
                        alerts and feeding
    dispatch            standby queue + a deterministic tick that fills idle
                        lanes
    clear-box           DESTRUCTIVE, superuser: clear an unsubmitted draft
                        (Ctrl-U)
    delivery            can this lane receive a message, and if not why
    flush               submit text left sitting in a pane's input box
    messages (queue)    direct messages queued and recently sent
    cancel-message (cancel)
                        drop a queued message
    metrics             read-only operations metrics as JSON
    panes               list terminal panes (possible targets)
    workspaces (tabs)   list workspaces and their tabs
    new-workspace (workspace)
                        create a named workspace (first tab + shell pane)
    new-tab (tab)       create a named tab in a workspace
    split               split a pane right or down into a new shell pane
    start-agent (agent)
                        launch an agent in a new pane, registered by name
                        (tracked on the herdr rollback)
    respawn-pane (respawn)
                        guardedly replace an existing managed pane's process
                        in place
    rename              rename a workspace, tab or pane
    focus               bring a workspace, tab or pane to the front
    close               close a workspace, tab or pane (kills what runs
                        inside)
    herdr               run any herdr subcommand through the daemon (rollback
                        backend only; refused under tmux)
    herdr-help          the rollback backend's own usage: command groups, or
                        one group's subcommands (refused under tmux)
    read                read recent output of a pane
    shutdown            stop the daemon (superusers only; dunks resume on next
                        start)
    serve               run the daemon in the foreground
    tui                 open the curses UI
    mcp                 run the MCP server on stdio (for agent harnesses)
    mcp-setup           show or apply MCP registration for agent harnesses
    guide (help, docs)  print the full guide (concepts, surfaces, protocol,
                        recipes)
    commands            list the socket/MCP command registry
    mcp-map             OLD flat MCP tool -> NEW grouped tool/action mapping

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --json                print raw JSON results
  --socket SOCKET       daemon socket path (default: $DUNKINGSHEEP_SOCKET or
                        ~/.config/dunkingsheep/dunkingsheep.sock)
  --self-pane SELF_PANE
                        pane id to use for target 'self' (default: $TMUX_PANE,
                        or $HERDR_PANE_ID on the rollback)
  --no-start-daemon     fail instead of auto-starting the daemon

Dunking Sheep types text (plus Enter) into terminal panes on a schedule.
Each schedule is a "dunk": a target pane, a text, an interval, and a running
flag. Dunks live in a background daemon, so the TUI, this CLI, the unix
socket and the MCP server all see and control the same dunks.

quick start
  dunkingsheep panes                              # what can I target?
  dunkingsheep add -T "Codex Site" -e 15 -t continue
  dunkingsheep add -T self -e 60 --only-idle --skip-if-unconsumed \
      -t "Check the backlog. If done: dunkingsheep remove {id}. Else keep going."
  dunkingsheep list                               # live status, ids, countdowns
  dunkingsheep remove d2
  dunkingsheep tui                                # the curses view of the same dunks

learn more
  dunkingsheep guide          full guide (concepts, MCP, socket protocol, recipes)
  dunkingsheep commands       every command the socket/MCP expose (--json: schemas)
  dunkingsheep <command> -h   per-command flags and examples

usage: dunkingsheep add [-h] [--target TARGET] [--text TEXT] [--every EVERY]
                        [--name NAME] [--only-idle] [--max-sends MAX_SENDS]
                        [--skip-if-unconsumed] [--ignore-typing] [--no-start]

Create a dunk that types TEXT + Enter into TARGET every EVERY minutes.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --target, -T TARGET   pane id, 'self', or a unique label substring
  --text, -t TEXT       text to send (default 'continue'); {id} etc. are
                        expanded
  --every, -e, --interval EVERY
                        interval: minutes, or e.g. 90s / 1.5h (default 10)
  --name, -n NAME       label for the dunk
  --only-idle           hold each send until the target agent is idle
  --max-sends MAX_SENDS
                        remove the dunk after N sends
  --skip-if-unconsumed  backpressure: skip a send if the previous one was
                        never picked up
  --ignore-typing       send even while someone is typing in the target's
                        input box (default: hold and re-check every minute)
  --no-start            create it stopped

examples:
  dunkingsheep add -T "Codex Site" -e 15 -t continue
  dunkingsheep add -T w8:p3 -e 1.5h -t "status report please" -n hourly
  dunkingsheep add -T self -e 30 --max-sends 1 -t "check CI now"
  dunkingsheep add -T self -e 60 --only-idle --skip-if-unconsumed \
      -t "If the backlog is done: dunkingsheep remove {id}. Else continue."
placeholders in TEXT: {id} {name} {count} {target} {interval} {time} {date}

Install a launcher so agents can run `dunkingsheep inbox read` as an ordinary

agent should and does refuse.

usage: dunkingsheep guard [-h] [--no-shadow]
                          [{status,install,install-tmux,uninstall,check,shadow,unshadow}]

Agents that call the terminal CLI directly bypass every protection in the daemon. On the herdr rollback backend the guard is a herdr wrapper, first on PATH, that routes exactly the four typing commands through the daemon instead. Every other herdr command is untouched.

positional arguments:
  {status,install,install-tmux,uninstall,check,shadow,unshadow}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --no-shadow           install the PATH wrapper only; do not take herdr's own
                        place (agents the herdr server starts itself will not
                        be covered)

new shells pick it up; existing panes need a fresh shell

usage: dunkingsheep inbox [-h] <subcommand> ...

Machine-to-machine messaging. A message is stored for the recipient agent to
read, so it cannot collide with a human typing, cannot stick half-sent, and
has no size limit.

positional arguments:
  <subcommand>
    count       how many messages are waiting
    send        put a message in an agent's inbox
    list        summaries of waiting messages
    read        read waiting messages and mark them read
    recover     replay the latest delivered batch after a lost read response
    archive     archive a mailbox in bulk (no deletion)
    status      state of one message by id
    ack         mark messages handled
    cancel      withdraw unread messages you sent
    delete      delete messages and their attachments
    stats       unread counts for every mailbox
    fetch       write an attachment to a local directory

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit

usage: dunkingsheep context [-h] <subcommand> ...

usage: dunkingsheep task [-h] <subcommand> ...

Tasks are global (fleet-wide) by default, or scoped to one pane. `task next`
claims atomically; `task follow` asks the daemon to push work to you when
idle.

positional arguments:
  <subcommand>
    add         create a task
    list (ls)   list visible tasks
    read        read one task in full
    update      change a task
    assign      assign a task (use 'self' for yourself)
    complete    complete a task for everyone
    block       mark a task blocked
    unblock     return a blocked task to the queue
    cancel      cancel a task
    delete      delete a task
    note        append an event to a task's history
    next        atomically claim the next task
    heartbeat   extend the lease on a claimed task
    release     give a claimed task back
    follow      receive pushed tasks when idle
    unfollow    stop receiving pushed tasks
    followers   list panes receiving pushed tasks
    stats       task counts by status
    metrics     task throughput, depth and latency (JSON)
    reap        requeue expired/dead leases now

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
